package.title: Slowing AI Could Speed Up the Economy
package.promised: An explanation of why deliberately slowing or adding human checks to AI workflows could make the economy more productive rather than less. I expect to learn where unchecked automation fails and why people may still be essential in the loop.

new_things: AI can create a second job of supervising the assistant meant to save time.
Less supervision could mean more finished work from existing models.
The speaker sees an economic opportunity in slowing the AI frontier.
Anthropic’s Dario Amodei has argued something relevant.
reports.held_question: Why would slowing the AI frontier reduce supervision and make the economy more productive?

new_things: Dario Amodei has argued for pacing frontier AI development.
The speaker thinks effort should go into systems that can actually finish work.
A model can seem impressive while still leaving the user to manage a checklist.
The important test is whether a handoff completes the work or just passes along the checklist.
reports.held_question: Will the handoff actually finish the work, or leave me holding the checklist?
